entities.name: Sextus Erucius Clarus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sextus Erucius Clarus, a prominent Roman senator and aristocrat of the 1st century CE, played a pivotal role in the governance of Rome during the reign of Emperor Antoninus Pius.

As Urban Prefect, Clarus oversaw the administration of the Roman Empire's vast territories, ensuring the stability and prosperity of the empire's vast provinces.

His twin consulship in AD 146 marked a significant milestone in his illustrious career, solidifying his position as a leading figure in Roman governance.
